questions.explanationHtml:
(b, d)
• In case of pure torsion the rate of change of angle of twist is constant along the length of the

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup: The Euler’s formula for the critical buckling load of a column assumes certain condition for its application. Which of the following assumption(s) is/are not part of the Euler’s buckling theory?
questions.questionText: The Euler’s formula for the critical buckling load of a column assumes certain condition for its application. Which of the following assumption(s) is/are not part of the Euler’s buckling theory?

options.html: The column is perfectly straight and has uniform cross-sectional area along its length.
options.text: The column is perfectly straight and has uniform cross-sectional area along its length.

options.html: The material of the column is perfectly elastic, and the stress-strain relationship follows Hooke’s law
options.text: The material of the column is perfectly elastic, and the stress-strain relationship follows Hooke’s law

options.html: The column experiences pure axial load, and no lateral forces are applied.
options.text: The column experiences pure axial load, and no lateral forces are applied.

options.html: The column is subjected to a bending load that causes bending before failure.
options.text: The column is subjected to a bending load that causes bending before failure.

questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
Euler’s buckling theory assumes that the column does not experience any bending before failure.
It assumes that the column will buckle elastically under the compressive load, which means the
column will undergo a sudden lateral deflection once the critical buckling load is reached.
